messages.subject: Scoping question
parts:
Suppose I create a Shiny app as a function ie:

myApp <- function(param) {

randomNumber <- sample(1:10,1)

ui <- fluidPage(
        h1(param))

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  x <- sample(1:10, 1)
  print(x * randomNumber)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

}

On Shiny Server I can create an app.R file with:

library(shiny)
myApp()

The scope of x is each session so it will be regenerated each view. In general variables defined outside of the server function are visible across sessions, but it is not clear if that is true in this case where the app is defined inside a function. 

What is the scope of `randomNumber` in the above example? When I experiment with Shiny Server `randomNumber` appears to be regenerated each session, but I could be wrong.

Kind Regards,
Carl

messages.author: 48725385c294169f
messages.subject: Re: Scoping question
parts:
First of all, I don't think that would be a valid app.R, as you're calling myApp without parameters.

randomNumber would be global, like any other variable declared within the myApp function. It's only variables within server that are specific to each session.

You can check this by printing randomNumber in server, and opening multiple sessions of your app.
